scenarios.name: docker-compose-postgres-hardened
scenarios.rationale: A meets every rubric item: pinned tag 1.23.2, POSTGRE_*/DJANGO_DB, LABEL_STUDIO_HOST, ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD} read from an untracked .env that is added to .gitignore, loopback binding, and DISABLE_SIGNUP_WITHOUT_LINK. B uses `:latest`, which the rubric explicitly forbids, and only leaves a comment saying to pin it. It also tells the user to paste a literal password into .env without adding .env to .gitignore. B's other points (loopback bind, signup disabled, extra hardening) are good but don't make up for the unpinned image.

scenarios.name: sdk2-create-project-import-predict
scenarios.rationale: Response B uses the 2.x SDK, reads the key from an env var, matches the control and tag names, and includes type, model_version and score. It correctly says the Client/start_project API is 1.x. Response A has the same code shape but labels it the 1.x API, which contradicts the rubric's 2.x requirement.

scenarios.name: rest-export-with-new-auth
scenarios.rationale: Both switch to a PAT exchanged via POST /api/token/refresh and call /export with exportType=JSON and download_all_tasks=true; B explicitly says to re-run the token step on a 401 and mentions the admin option to re-enable legacy tokens, both of which the rubric asks for. A only says the script fetches a new token on each run and omits the legacy re-enable option.
